# Kettle

### Team chat for people who get paged.

You already know what chat costs you. An incident starts in a DM, moves to a channel nobody was watching, and the postmortem gets written from memory three days later.

Kettle keeps the thread. Every alert opens its own channel, wired to PagerDuty and your deploy pipeline, and archives itself into a timestamped timeline the moment you close it. Nothing to copy into the doc afterward.

**What your engineers will notice**
Search that returns code as code, with syntax highlighting and a working line-jump to the repo. A desktop client that idles at 180 MB instead of 1.4 GB. Keyboard-first everything, including channel creation.

**What you'll notice**
Per-channel retention you set yourself, so legal stops emailing you about it. SCIM and SSO on every plan, including the cheap one. An export API that hands back JSON — not a zip of HTML you have to scrape.

**What it doesn't do**
No feed. No stories. No auto-summary of a conversation you were already in. If your team wants a social network, buy a different tool.

**Switching**
Imports from Slack and Teams preserve threads, files, and channel membership. Median cutover for a 200-person org is one weekend and one volunteer.

**Pricing**
$6 per user per month. No message caps, no enterprise upcharge to get audit logs.

**[Start a 30-day trial]** — no card, every feature on, delete the workspace when you're done.

---

~250 words. Kept one three-item list ("threads, files, and channel membership") and no "not just X, but Y."
